title: Compact objects transport along adjunctions whose right adjoint preserves coproducts
statement: Let C and D be preadditive categories whose Hom types lie in one fixed universe v. Let F:C→D and G:D→C be adjoint functors F⊣G, with F additive and G preserving coproducts indexed by every type in Type v. Suppose s is an object of C with the following finite-support property: for every type I in Type v, family X:I→C, coproduct cocone c of X and map f:s→c.pt, there are a finite subset J of I and maps g_i:s→X_i with f=∑_{i∈J} g_i followed by the ith injection. Then F(s) has the same finite-support property in D. Neither category is required to admit every coproduct. When fixed-universe coproducts exist this is exactly compactness [def-pc-compact-object], by the canonical comparison between finite-support and direct-sum-Hom bijectivity.

source.place: CategoryTheory.BrownRepresentability.IsCompactObj.of_adjunction, lines 56--67; compactness is the finite-support form of Stacks derived.tex, definition-compact-object

proof.text: For a coproduct cocone of objects X_j in D, preservation by G makes the mapped cocone a coproduct of G(X_j). Transpose a map F(s)→coproduct X_j across the adjunction. Compactness of s factors this transpose as a finite sum through the G(X_j). Transpose each summand back. Additivity of the adjunction Hom equivalence and its naturality identify the original map with the resulting finite sum through X_j. This is the existing complete source proof; no new theorem is postulated.
